finding.claim: An unauthenticated attacker can force a blocking outbound JWKS fetch on every request by sending tokens with random kid values, because a kid miss triggers get_signing_keys(refresh=True) with no rate limit or negative caching. This is an availability and amplification issue, not an authentication bypass.
finding.source: The kid field in the unverified token header, read at jwks_client.py:224-226 via decode_token with verify_signature=False.
finding.sink: Blocking HTTP request to the configured JWKS URI in fetch_data (jwks_client.py:117-121), triggered by get_signing_key refresh=True at jwks_client.py:203.

trace.note: get_signing_key_from_jwt decodes the header without verifying the signature
kid from the header is passed to get_signing_key
get_signing_keys() served from cache or fetched
match_kid finds no key for the attacker kid
cache miss triggers get_signing_keys(refresh=True), bypassing the cache
get_jwk_set calls fetch_data when data is None
urllib request to self.uri, blocking, with timeout

finding.guards_checked: kid is only compared for equality in match_kid (jwks_client.py:242) and never interpolated into a URL or path. The JWKS URI is application-configured, not token-derived. Its scheme is restricted to http/https (jwks_client.py:77-82). Signature verification runs after key lookup, so this is reachable pre-authentication. No negative cache or refresh rate limit exists.

finding.claim: Claim validation calls int() on signed-payload claim values but catches only ValueError, so values such as exp=Infinity (OverflowError) or iat=[1] (TypeError) escape as non-jwt exceptions. Access is still denied (fail-closed), so this is an error-handling inconsistency rather than a bypass, and it requires a validly signed token.
finding.source: Claim values in the payload, parsed by json.loads at api_jwt.py:298, which accepts Infinity/NaN and arrays by default. Reaching this path requires a token whose signature verifies.
finding.sink: int(payload[...]) in _validate_iat (api_jwt.py:477), _validate_nbf (api_jwt.py:492), and _validate_exp (api_jwt.py:506), each catching only ValueError.

trace.note: _decode_payload json.loads accepts Infinity/NaN and non-numeric JSON types
_jws.decode_complete verifies the signature before claims are validated
_validate_exp called when exp is present and verify_exp is set
int(payload['exp']) raises OverflowError for inf or TypeError for list, not caught by except ValueError at line 507

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification runs first (api_jwt.py:267), so the attacker must already hold a validly signed token. The failure raises an exception and grants no access. Non-numeric strings and NaN are caught as ValueError and converted to DecodeError (api_jwt.py:507-510).
